annotator_prompt.name: lifted_count
annotator_prompt.description: When several highlighted cubes shared a color, the recorded pickups progressed from robot-right to robot-left, whereas the stipulated increasing-world-x order assigned the count to different cubes. After a lifted cube was returned, the same count consequently selected an already-processed cube or the wrong remaining cube. This breaks SUFFICIENCY and makes the stipulated identity-based count update inconsistent with the observed pickups, breaking PREDICTABILITY. Replace the target ordering with red, green, blue, omitting unhighlighted colors, and within each color increasing world y, then increasing world x for ties. Determine this fixed order from highlight_frame, not from positions changed by handling. Keep the field as the number of distinct targets in this ordered prefix whose completed pickup lift has been observed. Initialize to 0; increment when the next target is visibly held off the table with TCP approximately z=0.15, not when grasping or commanding a lift. Preserve it through return, release, and retreat, and never count the same target again. For example, 2 means the first two targets in this corrected order have completed their lifts.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: lifted_count
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: With multiple highlighted cubes of one color, the old increasing-world-x order disagreed with the observed robot-right-to-left pickup order. Consequently a carried count could exclude the wrong identities after release and retreat, breaking SUFFICIENCY and PREDICTABILITY. Recover the fixed target order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue, omitting unhighlighted colors, then increasing world y within each color, with increasing world x only as a tie-breaker. Do not reorder using positions changed by handling. Initialize lifted_count to 0. Increment the carried value once only when this cycle visibly shows the next target in that fixed order held off the table after a lift with TCP approximately z=0.15. Use the current motion frames and held-cube identity to distinguish that new completion from a previously counted cube still being held. Do not increment for a low grasp, a commanded lift, an empty grasp, or an action executing no steps. Preserve the count through lowering, release, and retreat. For example, 2 excludes the first two targets in the corrected order from further pickup.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
Two systematic failures need correction. First, while approaching the button with button_pressed=false, the achieved hover TCP was displaced from the button center by roughly 1–1.5 cm. The policy closed at that displaced TCP with an upward nudge, then pressed using the same displaced x,y. The visible highlights had correctly been saved, but they did not establish a button press. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure in the geometric action rules, not missing historical information. Explicitly distinguish the achieved TCP from the object-centered waypoint. Before closing at hover and again before pressing, estimate the button center from the current calibrated views, using the wrist image to refine it. With open fingers at approximate button hover, command that button-centered x,y at z=0.15 and close on arrival. With closed fingers at approximate hover and no observed contact, descend directly to the newly estimated button-centered x,y at z=0.0075, keeping closed. Being approximately above the button permits the next operation; it does not imply that the achieved TCP x,y equals the button center. Retain contact recognition near z=0.024 and the closed retraction followed by opening. Apply the minimum-translation safeguard only after constructing the object-centered waypoint: if it already provides at least 2 mm translation, do not add an upward nudge; otherwise add a small upward adjustment within 5 mm. Remove any interpretation of 'same nominal approach waypoint' as copying the achieved TCP.

Second, after the highlights disappeared, multiple same-color targets were selected in an order inconsistent with the recorded pickups. After counted cubes were returned, this also led to regrasping them or redirecting away from the correctly approached next cube. This breaks SUFFICIENCY because lifted_count was interpreted against the wrong target order. Replace increasing-world-x same-color ordering everywhere with increasing world y, then increasing world x for ties, while retaining red-green-blue color priority. Establish this fixed order from highlight_frame and match individual cubes by position as well as color; robot-right is negative y and appears on the left of the front image. Interpret lifted_count as excluding the completed prefix of this order, including a newly completed lift recognized from this cycle. Select the next uncounted identity before testing whether the hand is aligned for descent. An open hover above a returned, counted cube must lead to an open approach to the next target at z=0.15, not a new grasp. Permit descent to z=0.02 and closure only when the open hand is approximately aligned over that selected uncounted target, allowing the existing approach-error tolerance. If already aligned over that target, descend rather than issuing another lateral hover. Keep the existing low-grasp lift, counted-cube return, open vertical retreat, and final-target holding rules. No additional memory field or generic preference for whichever highlighted cube happens to be beneath the hand is needed.

fields.name: highlight_frame
fields.description: Write null when memory is empty and no cube highlight has appeared. If the carried value is null, inspect all motion frames and store the earliest frame clearly showing white circular areas beneath the highlighted cubes. Ignore the white square beneath the button. Once a label is stored, carry it unchanged even when the white areas disappear. e.g. "E17"
fields.annotation: Initially null. On the first cycle containing visible white circular areas beneath cubes, store the earliest frame in that cycle clearly showing the highlighted set. Retain that label thereafter, including after the highlights disappear. The white square supporting the button is not a cube highlight. e.g. "E17"

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Initialize false. Set true when this cycle shows the closed fingertips down in contact with the button following a pressing descent, including a contact-limited TCP height around z=0.024. Otherwise preserve the carried value. Highlights alone do not establish a press. e.g. false
fields.annotation: Initially false. Set true at the first cycle showing the closed fingertips down in contact with the button after the pressing descent; the observed TCP may stop around z=0.024 rather than reaching the commanded z=0.0075. Keep true thereafter. Do not set true merely because highlights appear. e.g. false

Recover the highlighted identities and their fixed order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue, omitting unhighlighted colors; within each color use increasing world y, then increasing world x for ties. Do not reorder using positions changed by handling. The carried count excludes the completed prefix of this fixed order. Increment the carried count by one only when this cycle shows the next not-yet-counted target held off the table with TCP approximately z=0.15 after lifting. texts.action:
Start with an open hand and approach the button. Interpret all positions in world coordinates using the supplied camera calibration; estimate button and cube locations from their geometry, not raw image left/right. Use the wrist view to refine alignment. Recover target identities from highlight_frame after their white areas disappear, matching by position as well as color; never select every cube of a highlighted color. Use the observations of this cycle together with carried memory to recognize newly completed presses and lifts before selecting the action.

Button rules: If button_pressed is false and the hand is not yet above the button, move to its center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. At approximate button hover, allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm to proceed to the next operation, but do not treat the achieved TCP x,y as the button center. Before closing and again before pressing, estimate the button center from the current calibrated views, refining it with the wrist image. With open fingers at approximate hover, command that button-centered x,y at z=0.15 and close on arrival. With closed fingers at approximate hover and no observed contact yet, descend directly to the newly estimated button-centered x,y at z=0.0075 with fingers closed. Once contact is observed, retract to the button center at z=0.15, keeping closed; do not repeat the press merely because the actual contact height is higher than the command. After retracting, open at the button approach waypoint before traveling to a cube.

Pickup rules: Establish the fixed target order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue, then increasing world y within each color, with increasing world x for ties. Robot-right is negative y and appears on the left of the front image. Match individual identities by position as well as color; do not reorder using positions changed by handling. Interpret lifted_count as excluding the completed prefix, including any newly completed lift observed this cycle. Select the next uncounted identity before testing whether the hand is aligned for descent. With open fingers and adequate table clearance, approach its center at z=0.15. Use roll=3.1416, pitch=0 and a yaw aligned to its horizontal square edges, choosing the equivalent square orientation in approximately [-0.7854,0.7854]. Only when the open hand is approximately aligned above the selected uncounted target, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm; if already aligned, descend rather than commanding another hover. An open hand at hover above a returned, counted cube must instead approach the next uncounted target at z=0.15 with fingers open. With the cube grasped at low height, lift vertically to z=0.15 with fingers closed, preserving the aligned yaw. Estimate its grasp center from the visible cube and wrist geometry rather than treating a small TCP tracking error as a new target location.

Handling additional targets: Once a pickup lift is visibly complete, it counts even if the cube is subsequently returned. If another highlighted target remains and a counted cube is still held at hover height, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.01, retaining current orientation, and open on arrival. If the hand is low and open over that returned cube, retract vertically to approximately z=0.15 with fingers open before moving laterally. When retracted, approach the next uncounted target, not the cube just returned. After lifting the final target, keep it held; success should end the episode without requiring a placement.

For every gripper-only change, first construct the nominal object-centered waypoint rather than copying the achieved TCP pose. If that waypoint already provides at least 2 mm of translation from the reported TCP pose, do not add a nudge. Otherwise add a small upward adjustment within 5 mm so that the translation is at least 2 mm. Do not advance memory on an action that executed no steps. If alignment or grasp evidence is ambiguous, use the current wrist image to correct the relevant object-centered approach at safe height; a failed empty grasp should be retried without counting it. If no target evidence has yet been captured after the button operation, use a short bounded wait specifically to observe the highlight display and inspect every returned frame. Do not invent targets or repeatedly press a confirmed button. For an otherwise unmatched situation, preserve known task facts, keep a visibly held cube closed, and retract vertically to safe clearance before reassessing.

Do not reorder using positions changed by handling. The count is the length of the completed prefix of this order; increment only for the next target's completed lift, never again for a previously counted target.

edits.modify_from: Recover the highlighted identities from highlight_frame and order them red, green, blue, omitting unhighlighted colors; break same-color ties by increasing world x, then y.
edits.modify_to: Recover the highlighted identities and their fixed order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue, omitting unhighlighted colors; within each color use increasing world y, then increasing world x for ties. Do not reorder using positions changed by handling. The carried count excludes the completed prefix of this fixed order.

edits.modify_from: A low grasp is not a completed lift. A still-held previously counted target must not increment it again.
edits.modify_to: Use the current motion frames and held-cube identity to distinguish a newly completed lift from a previously counted target still being held. Do not increment for a low grasp, a commanded lift, an empty grasp, or an action executing no steps. A previously counted target must not increment it again.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If above the button at approach height with open fingers, close at the same nominal approach waypoint. If above it with closed fingers and no observed contact yet, descend to its center at z=0.0075 with fingers closed.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: At approximate button hover, allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm to proceed to the next operation, but do not treat the achieved TCP x,y as the button center. Before closing and again before pressing, estimate the button center from the current calibrated views, refining it with the wrist image. With open fingers at approximate hover, command that button-centered x,y at z=0.15 and close on arrival. With closed fingers at approximate hover and no observed contact yet, descend directly to the newly estimated button-centered x,y at z=0.0075 with fingers closed.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Order highlighted targets red, green, blue, with same-color ties by increasing world x then y. Select the first target not already represented by lifted_count.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Establish the fixed target order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue, then increasing world y within each color, with increasing world x for ties. Robot-right is negative y and appears on the left of the front image. Match individual identities by position as well as color; do not reorder using positions changed by handling. Interpret lifted_count as excluding the completed prefix, including any newly completed lift observed this cycle. Select the next uncounted identity before testing whether the hand is aligned for descent.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Once above that target, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm rather than repeatedly commanding the hover.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Only when the open hand is approximately aligned above the selected uncounted target, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm; if already aligned, descend rather than commanding another hover. An open hand at hover above a returned, counted cube must instead approach the next uncounted target at z=0.15 with fingers open.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Every gripper-only change must include at least 2 mm of translation if its nominal waypoint would otherwise equal the reported TCP pose; use a small upward adjustment, within 5 mm.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: For every gripper-only change, first construct the nominal object-centered waypoint rather than copying the achieved TCP pose. If that waypoint already provides at least 2 mm of translation from the reported TCP pose, do not add a nudge. Otherwise add a small upward adjustment within 5 mm so that the translation is at least 2 mm.
